title: A Si-on-SiC Platform for Interfacing with Vanadium Dopants in the Telecom O-Band
authors: Timothy Draher, Nolan Bitner, Vasileios Niaouris, Claire E. McDermott, David Czaplewski, Supratik Guha, David D. Awschalom, F. Joseph Heremans, Alan M. Dibos
abstract: Vanadium color centers in silicon carbide (SiC) offer telecom O-band emission, sub-microsecond optical lifetimes, and second-scale spin relaxation times, rendering them promising candidates for quantum network nodes. However, efficient photon extraction from the high-refractive-index SiC host remains challenging. Here, we introduce a silicon-on-SiC heterogeneous photonic platform in which silicon nanocavities evanescently couple to shallow vanadium dopants in commercial 4H-SiC, enabling efficient zero-phonon line (ZPL) collection under resonant excitation. In as-grown ensembles, we observe Purcell-enhanced photoluminescence with transient spectral hole burning linewidths of 50 MHz on microsecond timescales. In dilute implanted samples, we isolate individual vanadium centers with high-purity single photon emission and a Purcell-enhanced lifetime of 109 ns. The entire optical interface operates through a single lensed fiber, including a 905 nm repump laser that recovers the vanadium charge state with 95% efficiency. These results establish Si-on-SiC as a scalable, foundry-compatible platform for telecom-wavelength spin-photon interfaces.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Si-on-SiC platform designed to efficiently couple Vanadium color centers in SiC to optical cavities. By integrating silicon nanocavities, the authors overcome the challenge of photon extraction from high-index SiC, enabling high-purity, telecom-wavelength single-photon sources suitable for quantum network applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving efficient photon extraction from Vanadium color centers embedded in Silicon Carbide (SiC) for use in quantum network nodes operating at the telecom O-band.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a scalable Si-on-SiC platform that enables efficient zero-phonon line (ZPL) collection, achieving high-purity single-photon emission and Purcell-enhanced lifetimes.
method: The research involves heterogeneous integration of silicon nanocavities onto SiC substrates, coupled with time-resolved photoluminescence measurements and charge-state repumping using external lasers.
model_or_system: The system is a Si-on-SiC photonic platform hosting Vanadium ($	ext{V}^{4+}$) color centers in 4H-SiC. The structure couples the emitter's emission to silicon nanocavities to enhance photon collection into the telecom O-band.
key_observables: Zero-phonon line (ZPL) emission, Purcell-enhanced photoluminescence, single-photon emission purity, and transient spectral hole burning linewidths.
important_parameters: Telecom O-band ($	ext{1278–1388 nm}$), Purcell factor ($	ext{F}_{	ext{P}}$), cavity quality factor ($	ext{Q}$), and charge-repump efficiency ($95\%$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the feasibility of foundry-compatible fabrication processes and the ability to maintain the $	ext{V}^{4+}$ charge state via external repumping.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $	ext{V}$ dopant energy levels in $	ext{SiC}$ and schematics of the optical setup, detailing the coupling mechanism between the nanocavity and the dopants.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the fundamental physical challenge (photon extraction from high-index SiC) to proposing the Si-on-SiC heterogeneous platform, demonstrating enhanced ZPL collection in ensembles, and finally isolating and characterizing single emitters.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical realization of solid-state quantum emitters for quantum networking, providing a concrete, scalable platform for coupling quantum information sources to optical fibers.
